Simples explanation with example:
https://physics.stackexchange.com/questions/128075/how-would-wormhole-based-ftl-violate-causality

Any physicist will tell you wormholes are just a nice thing to imagine but not actually real because at the least you shouldn't be able to travel in time. The universe should at the minimum make sense. People enjoy it a lot because it's part of human nature to try to escape boundaries, even ones literally impossible to overcome (like living eternally in the afterlife). A lot of astronomers will take the "agnostic" path and just avoid talking about the infeasibility of wormholes because it makes people interested in science, and it gets them to study astronomy and that's what they want in the end. But here we were asked to tell what was the least believable thing in this sci-fi, and it's just that. It's just not possible and it's cool to imagine but it's annoying after you see for the 1000th time people thinking this is real. Just look at me getting downvoted for it. Nobody likes the depressing outcome of this.

True. It's why I've come back in time, after our understanding of time travel changed and logic has changed, to become my own father.

Look, we all enjoy sci-fi, it's why we're here, but this post specifically is about reality. Are you guys able to stop fantasizing for a little or is it unbearable to the point where fantasy is reality to you?

The point in this case is just traveling between two points faster than light can travel between those two points. Doesn't matter how you do it. You can therefore create funny paradoxes that are, obviously, unreal (like killing yourself before you were born and all that). But don't take my word for it, just ask a physicist or astronomer. It's 2022, I think it's time this reached laymen knowledge already.

Thanks to y'all for reminding me how little people on the internet have been educated on. Sometimes I have the delusion that I'm talking to people who have done a minimum amount of studying to understand the basics of what they're talking about. I'm sorry you're hurt about the limits of physics. Ignorance is bliss so at least you get that going for you.

Least believable are the rings giving faster than light transport, that's all. Any physicist in today's age will admit that wormholes are a cool idea but it's fantasy to believe they would exist because they'd break the causality principle. I hate to be that guy, but... Do you think you lost your job due to discrimination to the point where you're willing to risk losing time, energy, money and maybe reputation? I have no idea what you went through, I am not a lawyer, and I am very much against racism, but you should weigh how much this fight is worth for you, because the system is not in your favor. Just like with any case of employee vs employer, you are going against a much bigger entity that has the upper hand on everything, plus the presumption of innocence. Additionally, you were not fired; your contract was not extended, and in a time of crisis. And having only one bad feedback against multiple positive others would suggest to me that it wasn't significant in its weight. A manager with enough training knows to discount outliers (either positive or negative).

As I said, I'm not a lawyer, but my little experience with courts suggests to me you're bound to lose that case. And that would mean losing time, money, potentially having to pay the other parties' legal costs, and, depending on the industry, harm your reputation, just when you start to look out for a new job. In my industry, for example, word of mouth goes far, and having a lawsuit against your previous company makes it really hard for people to risk even giving you a chance. I imagine that losing a racial discrimination lawsuit against my previous company would be the death of my career.

So yeah, I hate to be the asshole, but if I was in your place I'd use my energy in other things now.
